lesson_title: The Level Sweep: Reading Markets Off a Graph
hook_text: Five rows of numbers hide the exact price where a market balances. Watch it surface.
clip_script: Now the classic task: determine the excess supply at twenty rand. This is the moment your graph stops being a picture and becomes a measuring instrument. Locate twenty rand on the price axis. Travel horizontally across the graph at that height. Your line strikes the demand curve first — drop straight down: quantity demanded is 100. Continue across to the supply curve — drop down again: quantity supplied is 200. At twenty rand, sellers offer 200 units while buyers take only 100. Quantity supplied exceeds quantity demanded by 200 minus 100 — 100 units. That gap is the excess supply. On the graph it is the horizontal distance between the two curves at the height of twenty rand.
visual_style: Table rows lifting off the page as glowing dots, curves threading through them, then a bright horizontal beam at R20 with the 100-unit gap illuminated between the lines.
pacing: Step-by-step build with a crisp payoff when the gap lights up and is measured.
